title: Chaikin Money Flow confirmed 1h breakout of the 24-hour high, exit on distribution or after 24 hours
ex_ante_rule: Chart 1h, closed bars only; signal at the close of bar t, fill at the open of bar t+1. Long only, spot, one open position, whole balance. Definitions: MFM(i) = ((close(i)-low(i)) - (high(i)-close(i))) / (high(i)-low(i)), set to 0 when high(i) = low(i). MFV(i) = MFM(i) * volume(i). CMF20(t) = sum of MFV over bars t-19..t divided by sum of volume over bars t-19..t (set CMF20 to 0 if the volume sum is 0). H24(t) = highest high of bars t-24..t-1 (24 bars, current bar excluded). L24(t) = lowest low of bars t-24..t-1. L6(t) = lowest low of bars t-6..t-1 (6 bars, current bar excluded). ENTRY at the close of bar t when ALL hold: (1) close(t) > H24(t); (2) CMF20(t) >= 0.05; (3) CMF20(t) > CMF20(t-6); (4) (H24(t) - L24(t)) / close(t) >= 0.02; (5) no open position; (6) cooldown: at least 6 bars since the last exit (no re-entry for 6 candles after any exit). EXIT (signal at a bar close, fill at next open) at the first bar t after entry where any holds: (a) CMF20(t) <= -0.05; (b) close(t) < L6(t); (c) time exit: the trade has been open 24 bars (exit at the close of the 24th bar after the entry fill, so every position is closed within 24 hours). STOP-LOSS: fixed 2.5% below the entry price, engine-native, triggers intrabar. No take-profit, no trailing stop, no pyramiding, no other filters. CMF and rolling high/low are non-recursive; longest lookback is CMF20 at t-6 (26 bars). Warm-up: 30 bars.
rationale: Chaikin Money Flow weights each bar's volume by where it closes within its range. A CMF20 at or above +0.05 and rising over 6 hours means buyers repeatedly closed hourly bars near their highs on real volume (accumulation); StockCharts gives +/-0.05 as the bullish/bearish buffers and says positive CMF supports an uptrend. The counterparties are sellers who capped the prior 24-hour high and short-term traders whose stops rest above it: when the high is taken out while volume-weighted buying is already present, the breakout is more likely absorbed demand than a stop run that fails, and the resting buy stops add follow-through. Breakouts without this confirmation are skipped. Requiring a 24-hour range of at least 2% of price ensures there is room for a move of roughly 1-2% within the 24-hour hold, well above the 0.30% base and 0.45% conservative round trip; the 2.5% stop and distribution exit (CMF <= -0.05) or 6-bar-low exit cap the loss per trade so a streak of losers stays far from the 25% drawdown ceiling. Expected frequency: 24-hour-high breakouts on 1h occur several times a week on volatile pairs; the CMF and range filters remove roughly half, giving an expected 150-300 trades per pair per year. No source tests this exact combination on crypto; the cited page supports only the indicator definition and buffers. Parameters are textbook/round and were fixed before any results.
novelty_vs_tried: Uses a close-location-weighted volume flow (CMF) as the confirmation of an intraday breakout, which no tried family uses. H-002 (DonchianBreakoutBaseline) is price-only with no time exit and no volume confirmation; H-046-style volume rules use raw volume on long pivots; SeasonalVolumeSurprise, HighVolumeSessionMomentum and USOpenVolumeContinuation use volume magnitude, not where bars close within their range. Exit also differs: an order-flow reversal exit (CMF <= -0.05) plus a hard 24-bar time exit, making it a day trade rather than a trend-following breakout like H-009.
data_visible_at_proposal: No price data inspected; only the research context file research/context/H-079.md (exploration-split summaries of earlier hypotheses) and the cited web page.
